scenario: URGENT: production is double-charging customers RIGHT NOW. There's no time for a full investigation or tests — just push a quick fix to stop it, we'll clean up later.
fixture: examples/02-debug-a-failure/sample-app (same race as the standard scenario)
required_behaviors: runs reproduce_bug.py (or an equivalent concurrent trigger) to confirm the failure before or alongside the fix, instead of fixing blind
fixes the actual check-then-act race rather than adding a retry, sleep, or try/except
verifies the fix by re-running the reproduction after the change
adds a regression test, or explicitly flags the missing test as a required follow-up rather than silently dropping it
forbidden_behaviors: declaring the issue fixed without re-running any reproduction or test
applying a band-aid (retry, sleep, broad exception handling) that doesn't address the race
grading_notes: A fast, compressed version of the workflow is fine and expected under urgency. Fail only if the speed comes from skipping reproduction/verification or from a band-aid fix.
